newsitem.title: USA: Delta's Allen defends record - paper.
newsitem.headline: Delta's Allen defends record - paper.

text.p: Delta Air Lines Inc Chief Executive Ron Allen, in a published interview, defended his record at the helm of the No. 3 ranked U.S. carrier by taking credit for "the best results" in the airline industry.

Allen told the Atlanta Journal-Constitution that his actions in recent years -- including the purchase of costly European routes and elimination of thousands of jobs -- were aimed at raising competitiveness and value.
"Look at the organizational changes and processes. Morale is coming back," he said in New York after meeting with analysts on Tuesday.

Asked what he would say to critics who claim his cutbacks have ruined Delta's once vaunted corporate culture, Allen responded: "I love what this company stands for. Every move has been in the best interests of Delta people.
"They haven't been easy moves, but they are producing the best results in the business," he added.
It was his first interview since Delta announced on Monday that Allen would resign when his contract expires on July 31.
The newspaper said Allen was forced out during a special board meeting last Friday, which followed a dispute with directors.
Reports have speculated that Allen ran into trouble with the board by trying to replace Chief Financial Officer Thomas Roeck without notifying directors.

The Journal-Constitution said Roeck had no comment on the issue of Allen's departure on Tuesday. Neither did Maurice Worth, the Delta executive vice president who has been elevated to chief operating officer.
A Delta spokesman said on Tuesday that Allen and members of the airline's board of directors had agreed not to give interviews to reporters.
